$$\left(\sum_{i=1}^{3n} a_i\right)^3 \ge k_n \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i a_{n+i} a_{2n+i}.$$

So $k_n = \inf \frac{(\sum a_i)^3}{\sum a_i a_{n+i} a_{2n+i}}$ over all non-decreasing non-negative sequences (not all zero).

Let me think about this. The sum $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i a_{n+i} a_{2n+i}$ picks out triples $(a_i, a_{n+i}, a_{2n+i})$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. These are "spread out" triples - the indices $i, n+i, 2n+i$ divide the $3n$ terms into three blocks of $n$.

By AM-GM, $(a_1+a_2+a_3)^3 \ge 27 a_1 a_2 a_3$ with equality when $a_1=a_2=a_3$. So $k_1 = 27$.
